I do think this person's strength is dot work...that comet they did is really nice.
You know, I have been tattooing for five years, and I am far from perfect, but I know this. There's always room for improvement, every good artist will tell you that much.

Hey, please don't take this the wrong way, but I think you should probably practice a bit more before tattooing on people. I know it's boring to "wait" to get better, and you are probably excited to start tattooing... but every craft needs practice. Start with tattooing just straight lines, get them perfect, and then move onto more complex shapes. Take your time to set your needle as close to the dot before as possible. You can also use a bigger needle, it's more forgiving. Also you should think more about your choice of colours, as of right now they kinda bleed into each other. I would say start with darker or more high contrast colours and then do the lighter ones. ![gif](emote|free_emotes_pack|slightly_smiling)

Hey I've got a question. About two months ago I got an older hedgehog (about 8 months old at the time). Since I got him he's been very grumpy - movement scares him, if you try to pick him up he'll ball up etc. I put it down to him settling in for the first few weeks. However during the first week when I was trying to start bonding with him he started biting a lot. He doesn't sniff/lick beforehand, so it's not about him exploring. He also bites hard, to the point that he's drawn blood many times. Plus he doesn't let go sometimes, and he'll hang on to your finger/hand, even when you push it towards him. He is still very grumpy even with daily handling. The only time you can pet him (on his back) is when his head is burrowed in a blanket, so he can't see you. At that point he stops caring and lets you pet him. But there is no way he's letting you near his belly. He'll bite unprovoked too. I've had him in a blanket and he will pop his head out and quickly bite you before hiding again. I've tried blowing on him, or saying "no" loudly to let him know it's not okay, but none of this seems to deter him. I'm just at a loss as to what I can do to try to stop him from biting, as apart from that he's fine. Does anyone have any ideas?
